comparison: Both strongly support the temporal window for plasticity (C4, C44, C82, C85, C86). OpenEval emphasizes dose-dependent effects and systematic temporal manipulation, while peer reviewers affirm this as 'a careful analysis' of 'early-life critical periods' without raising concerns about temporal specificity. OpenEval also includes C45 which peer reviewers group with morphological findings.

Both support the quantitative morphological and electrophysiological findings (C63, C64, C66, C67, C68). OpenEval includes C65 (comparable magnitude inference) not explicitly mentioned by peer reviewers. Peer reviewers include C45 (dose-dependence) which OpenEval groups with temporal window claims. Both accept the data without challenge.

Strong agreement on long-term consequences and dissociation between morphological recovery and persistent functional deficits (C46, C94-C100, C105-C106, C208). Peer reviewers call this 'an incredibly important finding' and OpenEval notes it is 'well-documented with appropriate statistics.' Both emphasize the key finding of recovered volume but persistent synapse loss. OpenEval also includes C6 not mentioned in peer review.

Both strongly support Draper's essential role in plasticity (C7, C114-C121). OpenEval emphasizes complete suppression with multiple RNAi lines and normal PN activity in knockdown animals (C118-C119). Peer reviewers describe this as 'compelling evidence' and 'an excellent mechanistic advance.' Peer review also includes C11 (intact terminals) which OpenEval addresses separately in R8.

Both support ensheathing glia-specific role (C48, C135, C138-C139, C145, C181-C182). OpenEval emphasizes cell-type specificity with complete suppression in ensheathing glia but not astrocytes. Peer reviewers accept this without challenge, noting glia 'infiltrate the VM7 glomerulus' and 'actively phagocytose OSN presynaptic terminals.' OpenEval includes additional claims (C127, C140) not explicitly mentioned by peer reviewers.

Both support glial infiltration and Draper upregulation (C8, C9, C49, C53, C150-C152, C155-C156). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative analysis and colocalization data. Peer reviewers affirm 'invasion of ensheathing glia into the glomerulus' without challenge. OpenEval includes additional claims about Draper-dependence of infiltration (C159-C161) which peer reviewers address separately in R12.

Perfect agreement on phagocytosis evidence using pHluorin reporter (C10, C54, C162-C166). OpenEval notes appropriate methodology with two independent RNAi lines. Peer reviewers accept 'compelling evidence' that glia 'actively phagocytose OSN presynaptic terminals' and are 'satisfied with the authors' responses' regarding synaptic readouts.

Both support the interpretation that intact terminals are engulfed (C12, C52). OpenEval emphasizes normal PN activity in knockdown animals as strong support, though notes direct visualization would strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this model without challenge. OpenEval includes C11, C51 and additional mechanistic claims (C118-C119) that peer reviewers partially address in R4. Peer review includes C171 which OpenEval addresses in R11.

Both support glomerular specificity with Or22a showing no changes (C90-C92, C211). OpenEval notes adequate sample sizes and appropriate comparison. Peer reviewers accept this as supporting evidence for VM7-specific mechanism without questioning the specificity. OpenEval includes C204 not mentioned by peer reviewers.

Perfect agreement on lack of astrocyte involvement (C129-C132, C188). OpenEval notes no suppression with astrocyte-specific knockdown contrasting with ensheathing glia effects. Peer reviewers accept this negative result as supporting evidence for ensheathing glia-specific mechanism without raising concerns.

OpenEval addresses comparison with mushroom body pruning literature and Draper's instructive role (C167-C175), noting this is reasonable speculation requiring additional experiments. Peer review R8 partially overlaps with C171 (distinction from debris accumulation models) and accepts this interpretation without challenge, though does not explicitly evaluate the speculative mechanistic claims.

Perfect agreement on membrane property controls (C103-C104). OpenEval notes this rules out non-specific effects on PN physiology. Peer reviewers accept this control data without comment, treating it as supporting evidence that activity changes are due to synaptic rather than intrinsic changes.

Overlap on Draper upregulation and colocalization (C159-C161). OpenEval includes these claims in broader evaluation of glial infiltration (R6), while peer reviewers address Draper upregulation separately. Both accept the data: peer reviewers explicitly state 'ensheathing glia increase Draper expression' and OpenEval notes 'statistical significance' and 'Draper enrichment on infiltrating membranes.'

OpenEval evaluates pupal exposure having no effect (C83-C84) and speculation about puparium barrier. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this supports the critical period specificity that peer reviewers affirm in R1.

OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN the slight difference in recovery kinetics (C101-C102) and speculation about LN plasticity, noting small sample sizes and need for additional experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN the speculative proposals for astrocyte functions (C133, C189-C190), noting these are hypotheses for future investigation without experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN the isoform-specific RNAi observations (C141-C143) showing partial effects with non-significant morphological suppression but full infiltration effects. Notes discrepancy requires additional experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports Brp density control data (C144) showing no differences across conditions, indicating entire terminal removal rather than selective synapse loss. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this supports the phagocytosis mechanism peer reviewers affirm in R7.

OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN the speculative hypotheses about functional significance for odor encoding (C215, C218-C220, C222), noting reasonable speculation but no direct experimental evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
